target: workflow.sh merge — the same refresh/preserve behavior holds with a '#' PREFIX (shell-style line file), including not misparsing a shebang line
cmd: source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/workflow.sh"; source "$FIXTURES/workflow-fixture.sh"; wf_file project.sh '#!/usr/bin/env bash' '# @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'echo "old greeting"' '# @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '# @agentic-loop:begin region=notes owner=project' '# my shell notes' '# @agentic-loop:end region=notes' 'echo done'; wf_file template.sh '#!/usr/bin/env bash' '# @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'echo "new greeting"' '# @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '# @agentic-loop:begin region=notes owner=project' '# upstream notes ignored' '# @agentic-loop:end region=notes' 'echo done'; VERDICT=$(workflow_merge project.sh template.sh '#' '{}'); BODY=$(cat project.sh); jq -n --argjson v "$VERDICT" --arg body "$BODY" '{verdict:$v, body:$body}'
_note: PREFIX is documented as the only language-specific knob; this case exercises it end to end on a shell file rather than assuming the '//' default generalizes. The shebang line ('#!...') contains the prefix but not the marker text, so it must survive as plain content — a scanner that matches on prefix alone rather than prefix+marker-text would misfire here.
